## PROVISIONAL DESIGN / own RELEASE — P-C proof-slice contract R1

Dylan Roy — delegated AI design. Actual OpenAI/Codex, the resumed original proof-view designer, receiver proof-slice-contract-designer-20261008, token PC-CONTRACT-DESIGN-R1-20261008T0243Z. Source/design exposed; backend/session continuity not independently attested; organizational-independence credit 0; scientific effect NONE. This delivers [offer6051101166](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/main/issues/281#issuecomment-6051101166) under actual [pickup6051114823](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/main/issues/281#issuecomment-6051114823).

**Recommendation:** v0 represents one explicitly complete, recorded ALL premise group per consuming unit and **refuses alternative routes**. It preserves every distinct use, its source-reading context and its own review binding. An independently pinned inventory is the expected set, not a count supplied by the candidate. This is a frozen engineering proposal, not an adopted schema, source-author validation, mathematical edge acceptance, reader implementation or completeness certificate.

### 1. Decision and exact scope

Two coherent alternatives were compared:

- **Explicit grouped alternatives:** each complete premise bundle concludes the same exact scoped statement, with separate applicability evidence and a source-reader determination of equivalence of conclusions. This is expressive, but neither the present 66-unit inventory nor the source responses establish such bundles or equivalence. It would require more authored semantics and consumer tests now.
- **Single-group v0, recommended:** zero or one group per unit; every recorded premise use of that unit belongs to its one ALL group. A second group, ANY, OR, a route selector, or a mixed partial bundle is refused. A later version can add alternatives after source/consumer agreement. The UI's proposed two-bundle rendering case therefore becomes a v0 refusal case, not an unimplemented success criterion.

"Complete group" means complete membership relative to the externally pinned, source-authored candidate-use inventory for this unit. It does not mean every mathematical premise has been discovered or validated. No truth-value evaluation, discharge, acceptance ranking, traffic-light colour or coverage percentage is computed.

The root is P Theorem C. C52 is a separately authored slice/root; no C52/R/C50/C51 premise edge is introduced here. The root retains fixed d>=2 and L>0, the normalized periodized Gaussian model, expected density per unit volume, all births/positive gap marks/separations, actual finite ordinary superlevel-H0 bars, essential-class exclusion, and the leading asymptotic only. Candidate-pair density and actual-elder density are distinct observables even when the stated leading coefficient agrees. CAP/E1/E2/REC remain its declared reading boundary.

No formal-coverage or numeric-certificate field is admitted in v0. A future formal mapping is separately versioned; the reader continues to say "not recorded" for this slice's formal lane. Counts and source identities are engineering metadata, not numerical mathematical certificates.

### 2. Closed contract notation and identities

The following is a normative data-contract draft, not implementation code or an executed JSON Schema. Every object lists **all** permitted keys; all listed keys are required. Additional keys are invalid. Null is allowed only where explicitly stated. Maps keyed by arbitrary IDs are not allowed; arrays carry explicit unique IDs. JSON duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, Boolean values in integer fields, duplicate IDs and unresolved references are invalid. Integers are nonnegative unless stated otherwise. Dates are RFC3339 UTC. Digests are lowercase hexadecimal; commits and Git blobs have 40 characters, SHA-256 has 64. IDs are case-sensitive, never reused for a different logical source unit or use.

FileIdentity = {
  repository: owner/name,
  commit: full commit,
  path: repository-relative file path,
  git_blob: full blob,
  sha256: SHA-256,
  bytes: integer
}

Paths reject absolute paths, traversal, empty components, backslashes and directories. The six fields are indivisible; repository and commit are **never inherited implicitly**, including for imports. A SourceRef resolves through one explicit SourceFile entry to that entire tuple. The same bytes at another commit do not authorize silently replacing the original tuple.

SourceFile = {id: ID, identity: FileIdentity}

SourceSelection = {
  source_id: SourceFile ID,
  lines: [positive first line, last line >= first] | null,
  locator: nonempty source-authored locator text,
  precision: "exact_lines" | "named_locator_unexpanded"
}

For exact_lines, lines is non-null. Extraction uses the authenticated original UTF-8 bytes, inclusive one-based LF-delimited lines, preserving their original bytes and line endings; no trimming, normalization or source execution. Sources containing CR line endings need a separately specified extraction version rather than silent normalization. For named_locator_unexpanded, lines is null: only the full file identity and the recorded locator are bound. The interface has not been resolved to an exact excerpt and must display that limitation. A named locator is not represented as a verified terminal proof.

Performer = {
  provider: string | null,
  agent: string | null,
  session: string | null,
  exposure: nonempty text
}

RecordIdentity is exactly one of:
- {kind:"github_comment_snapshot", repository, issue:positive integer, comment_id:decimal string, url, updated_at, body_bytes:integer, body_sha256:SHA-256}
- {kind:"github_review_snapshot", repository, pull_request:positive integer, review_id:decimal string, native_commit:full commit, url, submitted_at, body_bytes:integer, body_sha256:SHA-256}
- {kind:"git_file", file:FileIdentity}

A GitHub comment has **no native_commit field**. A SHA written in a comment is not a native review binding. Live mutable comment/review bodies must match their recorded raw UTF-8 body digest before use; otherwise show the pinned retained copy if one is available and authenticated, or refuse that evidence. Do not silently accept the edited live body. Git-file records use exact source-file bytes.

Record = {id:ID, identity:RecordIdentity, performer:Performer, role:"inventory"|"omission_read"|"author_response"|"applicability_review"|"design"|"withdrawal", scope:nonempty text}

RecordSelection = {record_id:Record ID, locator:nonempty exact heading/item selector}

SourcedText = {
  text:nonempty text,
  source_refs:SourceSelection[],
  record_refs:RecordSelection[],
  unknown_refs:Unknown ID[]
}

At least one source, record or unknown reference is required. SourcedText records an attributed assertion. Neither its wording nor its references establish that the assertion is true. A statement lacking a recorded applicability explanation keeps an explicit unknown rather than borrowing one from another use.

### 3. Closed slice, unit and per-use objects

ProofSlice = {
  schema:"proof-slice/v0-provisional-1",
  artifact_kind:"source_companion",
  id:ID,
  read_at:UTC,
  author:Performer,
  scientific_effect:"NONE",
  status_authority:false,
  independence_credit:0,
  root:Root,
  sources:SourceFile[],
  records:Record[],
  inventory_binding:InventoryBinding,
  units:Unit[],
  suppliers:Supplier[],
  unknowns:Unknown[],
  history:HistoryEvent[],
  recorded_counts:RecordedCounts
}

Root = {
  statement_id:ID,
  source_statement:SourceSelection,
  entry_unit_ids:Unit ID[],
  graph_node:string|null,
  museum_card:string|null,
  semantics:{
    model:SourcedText,
    observables:SourcedText[],
    normalization:SourcedText,
    parameters:SourcedText,
    limit_order:SourcedText,
    conclusion:SourcedText,
    exclusions:SourcedText[]
  },
  reading_boundaries:ReadingBoundary[]
}

ReadingBoundary = {
  id:ID,
  source_id:SourceFile ID,
  consumed_lines:[first,last][],
  excluded_lines:[first,last][],
  reason:SourcedText
}

Root entry_unit_ids is nonempty, source-authored, and resolves inside the full expected inventory. It identifies the exact concluding units for the selected statement; the designer does not choose them by title similarity.

The imported reading sets do not become independent theorem premises merely by being listed. Per-use source_reading identifies where the correction/boundary applies. Source authors decide those links. Consumed selections must be within the allowed ranges and outside all exclusions; ranges are ordered, bounded by the authenticated source and non-overlapping within each list. CAP must retain the l30-47 exclusion; showing only its broad 1-168 envelope would lose N6. The present recorded deterministic CAP selection is l11-28 and l49-167. REC's Theorem-A cylinder bound is not silently imposed on every covariance r0 use.

Unit = {
  id:ID,
  source:SourceSelection,
  section:integer,
  description:SourcedText,
  uses:Use[],
  premise_groups:PremiseGroup[],
  related_unit_ids:Unit ID[]
}

PremiseGroup = {
  id:ID,
  combination:"ALL",
  conclusion:Unit ID,
  premise_use_ids:Use ID[],
  basis:RecordSelection[]
}

A unit has at most one group. The group's use IDs equal **exactly** that unit's uses whose kind is premise: no omission, duplicate, extra use, cross-unit borrowed use or second group. Zero premise uses requires zero groups; an empty ALL group is invalid. Every non-premise use remains visible outside the group. The mapped inferential graph is conclusion-unit -> premise-group -> supplied inventory units; the consuming unit/source also remains attached as the location of the argument. Reject a cycle in this mapped inferential graph. Context/history/related-unit links are not traversed as premises. An unexpanded imported interface cannot certify that no hidden cycle exists; the E2/P10 non-circularity question remains source-reader work. related_unit_ids is explicitly non-inferential navigation. A zero-use display/lead-in is still an inventoried unit; its zero uses cannot certify a self-proving result. The group conclusion must be a unit in the same full inventory; its mathematical correspondence is source-authored.

Use = {
  id:ID,
  kind:"premise"|"context"|"reading_correction"|"scope_guard"|"check",
  binding:UseBinding,
  provenance:RecordSelection[],
  applicability_reviews:ReviewBinding[],
  unknown_refs:Unknown ID[]
}

UseBinding = {
  consumer_statement_id:Root statement ID,
  consumer_unit_id:Unit ID,
  consumer_source:SourceSelection,
  supplier_ids:Supplier ID[],
  claimed_interface:SourcedText,
  parameter_mapping:SourcedText,
  context:SourcedText,
  source_reading:ReadingUse[]
}

ReadingUse = {
  boundary_id:ReadingBoundary ID,
  supplier_ids:Supplier ID[],
  applies_to:SourceSelection[],
  explanation:SourcedText
}

Supplier = {
  id:ID,
  kind:"inventory_unit"|"source_section"|"import"|"external"|"unnamed",
  unit_ids:Unit ID[],
  source_refs:SourceSelection[],
  external_ref:ExternalReference|null,
  interface:SourcedText,
  expansion:"in_slice"|"unexpanded",
  unknown_refs:Unknown ID[]
}

ExternalReference = {
  title:string,
  authors:string[],
  edition_or_version:string|null,
  theorem_or_section:string|null,
  url:string|null,
  retained_record:RecordSelection|null
}

For inventory_unit suppliers, unit_ids is nonempty and each resolves against the **external expected inventory**; in a complete slice its Unit records are present. Source_section/import suppliers have authenticated source_refs and remain unexpanded unless their actual derivation is included in the slice. External and unnamed suppliers remain visibly unexpanded. Unknown bibliographic facts are null, not guessed; an unresolved external reference has a linked Unknown. An unnamed mechanism is not given an invented theorem identity. Shared suppliers have one Supplier record, but **every Use has its own binding and evidence**.

ReviewBinding = {
  record:RecordSelection,
  reviewed_use:ResolvedUseSnapshot,
  scope:SourcedText,
  disposition_as_recorded:string,
  limitations:SourcedText[],
  later_disposition_records:RecordSelection[]
}

ResolvedUseSnapshot is a closed expanded snapshot with keys {consumer_statement_id, consumer_statement_source, consumer_semantics, consumer_unit_id, consumer_source, suppliers, claimed_interface, parameter_mapping, context, source_reading}. consumer_statement_source and consumer_semantics are the exact source/semantic fields of the reviewed Root. The other fields are the reviewed UseBinding fields, expanded by these fixed rules:
- Every SourceSelection.source_id is replaced by file:FileIdentity; all its other keys remain.
- Every RecordSelection.record_id is replaced by record:RecordIdentity; locator remains.
- supplier_ids is replaced by suppliers containing the complete expanded Supplier objects.
- Each ReadingUse.boundary_id is replaced by boundary containing the complete expanded ReadingBoundary; its other supplier/source/text fields are expanded as above.
- unknown_refs is replaced by unknowns containing the complete referenced Unknown objects (id, description, affects_use_ids, provenance), recursively expanded under these same rules. Unknown-reference cycles are invalid.
- Unit IDs remain IDs, and every inventory-unit Supplier must include its exact source selection. No source, supplier, boundary or record lookup against the current candidate is permitted inside a stored reviewed snapshot.

Thus the expanded type is mechanically specified, has no extra keys, and has no mutable ID-table indirection. The review record must carry or bind this original target snapshot. At comparison time expand the CURRENT use independently and compare it with the STORED reviewed snapshot. Do not re-expand an old use's IDs through today's supplier table, and do not fill absent historical target facts with current values. If an older record supplies insufficient target identity, attach it as attributed provenance rather than a machine-reusable ReviewBinding.

The record must actually identify the reviewed use/scope. Equality of the stored reviewed_use and independently expanded current ResolvedUseSnapshot is necessary for reuse and never sufficient for mathematical applicability. Compare the consumer statement/step, both complete source identities and selections, supplied interface, substitutions, context and reading amendments. Supplier ID, file digest, navigation seen-set or provider name alone cannot key reuse. Original review identity and disposition are preserved. Changed/superseding/withdrawn dispositions remain separately linked. A statement-level or omission review must not be fabricated into a use-specific ReviewBinding. Empty applicability_reviews means no such use-bound assessment is attached; it does not declare the implication false.

Unknown = {id:ID, description:SourcedText, affects_use_ids:Use ID[], provenance:RecordSelection[]}

Each Unknown description has at least one source or record basis and cannot refer to itself; reject unknown-reference cycles. An example-local missing annotation is labeled as such and is not promoted into a reported mathematical gap.

HistoryEvent = {
  id:ID,
  kind:"inventory_statement"|"omission_observation"|"author_inventory_amendment"|"applicability_observation"|"supersession_note",
  record:RecordSelection,
  affects_unit_ids:Unit ID[],
  affects_use_ids:Use ID[],
  text:string
}

No event kinds named accepted, proved, closed or audited are admitted. Historical words such as PASS or "I accept A1-A6" may be quoted in text with their exact scope; they do not become computed edge states. An inventory-author amendment remains an inventory amendment.

RecordedCounts = {
  units:integer,
  uses:integer,
  premise_uses:integer,
  nonpremise_uses:integer,
  unknowns:integer,
  basis:RecordSelection[]
}

These are quoted as dated recorded inventory counts. The structural validator may compare them with exact membership but does not turn them into scientific coverage. 66 source blocks and 115 proposed uses (114 inferential + one check in correction6049640627) are not a count of atomic mathematical premises. Extra source-reading annotations are not silently added to those 115 use IDs.

### 4. Independent expected inventory and refusal of coherent deletion

InventoryBinding = {
  expected_inventory:FileIdentity,
  extraction_record:RecordSelection,
  correction_records:RecordSelection[]
}

The future expected-inventory JSON is a **separate pinned source object**, produced from the existing inventory and accepted inventory amendments, not regenerated from the candidate ProofSlice. It is proposed beside the companion under Math- reviews/, outside sealed packets. Its closed shape is:

ExpectedInventory = {
  schema:"proof-unit-inventory/v0-provisional-1",
  root_statement_id:ID,
  root_boundary:Root,
  source:FileIdentity,
  sources:SourceFile[],
  records:Record[],
  unknowns:Unknown[],
  extraction:{
    rule:"maximal-contiguous-nonempty-nonheading-blocks",
    heading_boundaries:[310,482],
    payload_lines:[312,480],
    line_convention:"one-based-inclusive-original-LF"
  },
  expected_units:[{id:ID,section:integer,lines:[first,last]}],
  expected_uses:[{id:ID,consumer_unit_id:ID,kind:Use kind}],
  provenance:RecordSelection[]
}

ExpectedInventory carries its own source/record/unknown tables. All Root/provenance references resolve inside those pinned tables, never through the candidate slice; expected-unit/use/unknown affected-ID references resolve against its own expected sets. Its source field equals the P entry in its sources. Root comparison uses fully resolved immutable values, not merely equal local IDs.

ExpectedInventory is not a status authority. Its candidate use memberships/kinds remain descriptive and revisable through explicit source-author/reader records. Its first materialized file and digest do not yet exist; **this design invents neither**. The actual inventory author must validate that materialization and its source semantics.

The loader's trusted inputs are: the candidate slice, authenticated expected-inventory bytes, and an expected-inventory FileIdentity supplied **outside the candidate** by the approved source/consumer release. The candidate's declared InventoryBinding must equal that external identity. For the site, pin the slice and the expected-inventory copy separately in PROVENANCE.json, with the existing consumer's independently fixed release identities; do not accept a candidate-selected manifest or fallback inventory. The expected inventory itself must carry the fixed P source identity and the frozen inventory/review/correction references below.

Compare ordered exact unit tuples (ID, section, line range), exact use-ID/consumer/kind membership and root boundary against that trusted inventory. Counts are derived cross-checks, never the anchor. This detects deleting B02 and reducing blocks to65, deleting U01.3 and reducing uses to114, and same-count substitution, even if all candidate-local counts agree.

Changing both candidate and expected-inventory files cannot defeat the independent expected digest. Deliberately approving a new external trust root is a new reviewed source/consumer change, not something cryptography or this schema forbids. There is no claim to detect a coordinated authorized replacement of all trust anchors.

Materializing this proposed expected file is a later task that reuses the existing B01-B66 locators and the six accepted inventory additions. It does **not** repeat the proof extraction. The already recorded per-section denominator remains 11/10/8/19/5/13. The original inventory artifact body is separately identified by its published 21041B / 9b068ab9531675e5f7477b50872531d6338ba7566513fab9fbfcc9915ba87049 digest; that is not the digest of the entire GitHub delivery comment.

### 5. Explicitly partial real-inventory example

This is a **two-unit design example**, not a ProofSlice, not the independently pinned expected-inventory file and not consumable by the production slice loader. It demonstrates existing B01/B02 and A1's added U01.3. B03-B66, 112 other use entries, all five reading-boundary records, external imports and the complete unknown inventory are omitted from the example. Their omission here has no completeness meaning.

All P selections in this example resolve to this full tuple:

- repository d6g8k5htny-coder/Math-
- commit 9fd261135b41daf1e377f9ef2db193fee6ec36be
- path imports/lifetime_parent_20260925/UNIFORM_MATRIX_CAP_AND_LIFETIME.md
- git_blob dfed3b8d318a3ab1950957f393307733a4bef3f2
- sha256 9350ad6eaba6626b93c3dedeef9e2ff816e5cdf1c8318e85fb27499141c84bc7
- bytes 40261

Proposed stable root statement key: UNIFORM-MATRIX-CAP-LIFETIME-20260924-v1::Theorem-C. This separates a statement from its exact P file/version. It does not rename the existing graph node.

**B01:** source P l312, section10. Description attributed to inventory B01: defines pi_r and leads to (10.1). Its candidate group G-B01 has combination ALL, conclusion B02, and exactly [U01.1,U01.2,U01.3]. The membership is the inventory plus A1's source-author response, not an applicability verdict.

**B02:** source P l314-315, section10. Description attributed to inventory B02: (10.1) conclusion, not a second derivation. uses=[] and premise_groups=[]. Its related_unit_ids=[B01] records display navigation only. Its zero-use form is retained in the external 66-unit denominator.

**U01.1**
- kind premise; consumer statement key above, unit B01, exact consumer source P l312

- context: B01's definition of pi_r leading to (10.1), as the inventory records
- source_reading=[] in this partial example; no E1/REC per-use applicability is invented for this particular entry
- provenance: inventory6049443374/B01/U01.1
- applicability_reviews=[]; earlier P proof imported/unexpanded, with inventory UNKNOWN-U1 retained

**U01.2**
- same exact consumer identity; kind premise
- supplier S-unnamed-linear-density: unnamed, source_refs=[], external_ref=null, expansion unexpanded
- claimed interface: unnamed invertible-linear observation density rule, verbatim inventory designation; no named external theorem supplied
- parameter mapping: "Not separately recorded"; example-local mapping unknown
- context: the same B01 definition/conclusion context, with its own provenance reference
- source_reading=[]; provenance inventory6049443374/B01/U01.2; applicability_reviews=[]
- unknown: supplying derivation and precise applicability are unexpanded in this example; this is not a refutation

**U01.3**

- claimed interface: the factor 12 r^(-(d+3)) in (10.1), as omission A1 and author response record
- parameter mapping: the determinant of the same observation transformation consumed by B01/B02; this is an attributed reading from A1, not a fresh designer verification
- context: supplies a separately counted factor absent from the original 109-use listing
- source_reading=[]; provenance omission6049548422/A1 plus author6049640627/A1; applicability_reviews=[]
- unknown: earlier P derivation remains unexpanded

All three use bindings remain distinct. Their source-sharing does not share a review. The author response's acceptance of A1 as an **inventory addition** is recorded by HistoryEvent kind author_inventory_amendment; it does not populate applicability_reviews or an accepted-edge field. The omission reader's text-level checks elsewhere are not fabricated into mathematical acceptance of these three inferences.

The example's exact record identities are the full-body snapshots in §8: inventory6049443374, omission6049548422 and correction6049640627. The recorded performers are, respectively, OpenAI/Codex root chat01a103c8-7a8e-7461-8e9f-36e3b02757c5; Grok Bot agent10, a non-Claude/nonauthor support reader; and that same OpenAI inventory author. Their disclosed source exposure and zero organizational-independence credit remain attached. This designer is none of those historical performers.

### 6. Discriminating cases to implement later — NOT executed tests

| Mutation/control | Required engineering result | Mathematical responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Delete B02 and lower every candidate-local count consistently | Refuse against the independently pinned exact B01-B66 tuple list; zero-use units remain required | Source owner/omission reader establish that denominator |
| Substitute B67 for B02 or retain B02 with different lines | Refuse exact ID/locator mismatch, despite count66 | Locators initially validated by source inventory process |
| Delete U01.3 and lower local use totals | Refuse exact amended expected-use membership | A1 remains an inventory correction, not edge acceptance |
| Remove U01.2 only from G-B01 | Refuse: group must equal B01's complete premise-use set | Whether those uses suffice is not checked |
| Change ALL to ANY/OR, add a second group or hide alternative_route in an extra key | Refuse unsupported field/value/cardinality; do not flatten, mix or choose a route | A future alternatives version needs source-conclusion equivalence evidence |
| Reclassify U66.3 as a premise or silently include it in a group | Refuse mismatch with amended expected-use kind; show it as a check | R1/source response controls the recorded classification |
| Reuse a B09 supplier review for another consuming statement/context/substitution, or mutate the supplier table while keeping its ID | Refuse reuse when fully resolved ReviewBinding target differs; still show original record | A reader assesses the new use; supplier bytes alone prove nothing |
| Change a consumed source/line range/reading amendment while retaining an old ReviewBinding | Keep old review as historical, report no matching use-bound assessment | Source author/reader decide new applicability |
| Change only an unrelated repository tip or UI order, preserving all recorded source identities and use bindings | Do not invalidate the original source review merely for tip drift; deterministic display still applies | Fresh candidate CI remains separately required if implementation changes |
| Omit repository/commit on an import, forge a comment-native commit, substitute correct bytes under an unbound commit | Refuse missing/extra fields or unauthenticated file membership | Identity is not scientific sufficiency |
| Add CAP l30-47 to a consumed selection | Refuse declared selection/exclusion conflict; retain exclusion visibly | Source reader validates consumption boundaries |
| Replace per-volume P-C with whole-torus C52 occurrence in root semantics | Refuse mismatch with externally fixed root boundary; no fuzzy title-based join | Source author validates the root boundary; schema alone cannot understand arbitrary prose |
| Remove an unknown/unexpanded marker or render an unresolved supplier as a proved leaf | Consumer regression fails; no terminal-proof representation for unexpanded/unknown suppliers | Missing derivations remain matters for source readers |
| Change a mutable evidence comment body while keeping its old identity | Refuse raw-body digest mismatch or display an authenticated retained version | Later disposition is separately recorded, never silently rebound |
| Label #392's weaker conditional little-o statement as closing the stronger rate | A curated source fixture can reject altered rendering; generic schema cannot diagnose arbitrary overclaiming text | Source-author and independent reader validate the exact stronger/weaker distinction |
| Provide the two-unit example as production ProofSlice | Refuse incomplete shape/membership and missing external expected-inventory pin | No demonstration is promoted into coverage |

A proposed failure case is not an executed regression, a detected product defect or a theorem argument. The current graph/profile/conditional pilot is not alleged to fail these cases.

### 7. Maintenance, remaining agreements and rollout

**Source/inventory author or explicitly delegated source custodian:** validate the expected-inventory JSON materialization, exact root semantics, source locators, candidate use kinds/groups, reading amendments and per-use applicability. Reconcile later U2/U3/U4/I2 work at its own source identities; the old unknown history is preserved, not silently relabeled by this draft. This author is presently doing separate I2 proof work; no pickup or interruption is inferred.

**Separate source reader:** audit missing/incorrect dependencies and applicability, including unnamed mechanisms. The existing omission read is retained at its exact scope. It is not a blanket certification of 115 implications.

**Actual UI author:** agree or amend this closed consumer shape and the choice to refuse alternatives in v0; preserve source-sharing with distinct uses, all unknowns, source exclusions and dated counts. Implementation is one serialized increment **after9/10**, in a separate claimed/reviewed PR. Neither9 nor10 waits on this design.

**Engineering implementer/reviewer:** validate strict shape, source authentication, external inventory trust, deterministic joins, negative cases and non-mutation. Reuse the existing source-reference/conditional-route/profile interfaces where suitable. The separate retrofit source-authentication repair must be consumed only after its actual disposition; a JSON-valid record is not authenticated merely because the older checker accepts it.

Outstanding concrete decisions:
1. Source author: are this v0 grouping/identity model and the example's candidate grouping faithful enough to materialize, and which exact artifact first owns the independently pinned inventory?
2. UI author: agree to single-group v0 refusal of alternatives and the external two-artifact pin, replacing the earlier two-bundle rendering expectation?
3. Separate source reader: which exact omission/applicability review can cover the materialized record without duplicating ongoing I2 or other proof work?

These are affected-source/consumer decisions, not a vote by every unrelated agent. No implementation starts from this design delivery.
